claims.text: The modified material is an equimolar WTaTiVZr high-entropy alloy.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy is single phase.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has pronounced atomic-scale lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion modifies dislocation-core configurations in BCC solid-solution HEAs.
Lattice distortion lowers the activation barrier for dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion lowers the activation barrier for dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion produces a more balanced mixture of edge and screw dislocations than in conventional BCC metals.
The resulting edge-and-screw dislocation population is more mobile.
Lattice distortion creates heterogeneous local stress fields through local variations in atomic spacing.
Distortion-enabled dislocation rearrangement reduces dislocation pile-up and delays crack initiation.
Pure tungsten predominantly retains high-activation-energy screw dislocations under the specified high-temperature conditions.
WTaTiVZr will have a lower critical stress for initiation of dislocation motion than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will sustain greater plastic strain before failure than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit delayed crack nucleation relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit less creep displacement than pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
The proposed lattice-distortion mechanism applies approximately from 700 to 900 degrees Celsius, where diffusion and dislocation dynamics are active.
Grain-boundary effects, secondary phases, and impurities can obscure the isolated contribution of lattice distortion.
Matching grain size, impurity levels, and processing history between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten makes lattice distortion the only experimental variable.

In-situ nanoindentation or micropillar compression between 700 and 900 degrees Celsius can measure activation stress, dislocation character, creep displacement, and crack initiation in both materials.
Prior atomistic work supports distortion-induced changes in edge-dislocation configurations in compositionally complex BCC alloys.

contradictions.description: The comparison changes elemental composition from pure W to a five-element alloy, so matching processing, grain size, and impurities cannot make severe lattice distortion the only variable.

The hypothesis predicts lower barriers and greater dislocation mobility while also predicting reduced creep displacement, but it gives no countervailing strengthening mechanism that reconciles easier thermally activated motion with improved creep resistance.
